scenarios.title: Mark traffic at a boundary without erasing other labels
scenarios.summary: Repair the boundary labels while preserving the independent report stream.
scenarios.objective: Rewrite every office-interactive packet to DSCP 46. Rewrite every untrusted office-guest packet to DSCP 0, regardless of its incoming label. Preserve the incoming DSCP on office-report; it varies between supplied packets. Deliver every packet in all three packet patterns. Queue priority is not required for this boundary-label task.
hints: Read incoming labels, chosen queue and actual results separately; a larger DSCP number is not a priority rank.
Inspect every failed packet pattern and preserve the streams named in the task. Do not hide a delay failure by dropping packets.
Use the optional worked policy only when you want the full explanation; several supported queue sizes or non-high guest labels can be valid.
scenarios.simplifications: Sources checked 2026-11-02: CCNA current v1.1/4.7 and RFC2474. Supplied named-flow classification only, equal-size packets, integer teaching slots, one packet per slot, explicit two-queue strict priority or FIFO, finite waiting buffers and tail drop. No host packets, network, clock, IOS, arbitrary header filters, variable serialization, fairness guarantee, RED/WRED/ECN, policing, shaping, TCP or end-to-end guarantee. This is a narrow practical slice, not complete QoS/exam preparation.

scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare the required outcome with actual labels, queue, drops and waiting in the failing packet pattern. Keep correct checks; change one policy decision and rerun.
scenarios.explanation: The reference is one supported policy, not a required command string. Classification and marking happen before queue selection; explicit mappings determine priority. Finite buffers and a one-packet-per-slot link derive actual departures and drops. All deterministic packet patterns are checked, and edits clear the tested result. Equivalent policies are accepted when every required outcome holds.

scenarios.title: Protect interactive packets when a shared link is busy
scenarios.summary: Repair queue selection so interactive packets wait less without losing reports.
scenarios.objective: Let every uplink-interactive packet begin transmission in its arrival slot: zero queue waiting in all three packet patterns. Deliver every uplink-report packet and preserve all incoming DSCP labels. Use at most the supplied eight waiting places across both queues. One equal-size packet can be transmitted per virtual slot; slots are not milliseconds.
hints: Read incoming labels, chosen queue and actual results separately; a larger DSCP number is not a priority rank.

scenarios.title: Hand over a trusted queue policy without starving other traffic
scenarios.summary: Repair trust, queue capacity and delivery together across the supplied packet patterns.
scenarios.objective: Mark branch-interactive as DSCP 46 and give every packet zero queue waiting in all three packet patterns. Keep every branch-guest packet outside the high queue and deliver all of them. Any outgoing guest label that satisfies that policy is acceptable. Preserve every incoming label on branch-report and deliver every report packet. Share no more than eight waiting places between the queues. Do not solve a delay problem by dropping the delayed traffic.
